street.methodSummary: Every multiple we could confirm is EV/EBITDA on pre-IndAS (after-rent) EBITDA 1.5-2 years forward: Motilal Oswal 49x Sep-28E, Emkay 56x Jun-28E, Equirus 58x, Jefferies and Elara 50x FY28E; JM Financial (DCF, 53x implied) and ICICI Securities (DCF, ~48x India implied). Nobody uses P/E or EV/Sales as the main method; Bloomberg consensus P/E was 119x / 87x one/two-year forward (Motilal Oswal, 9-Sep-2026).

ownership.trend: The six-month lock-up on pre-IPO shares ended on 8-May-2026 and the sovereign and venture investors began to sell: block deals of at least 8.15 cr shares at ₹473 that day (Alpha Wave, KKR's Birdseye View, TR Capital and others; buyers included Citi, BlackRock, Fidelity, HDFC MF and ICICI Pru MF), SoftBank 5.65 cr shares (3.25%) at ~₹509 on 3-Jun and a reported ADIA block of 4 cr shares at ₹490 on 11-Jun. Foreign institutions went from 4.3% (Mar-2026) to 12.8% and Indian institutions from 15.5% to 23.6% by Jun-2026. In the September quarter SoftBank sold another 4.5 cr shares at ₹642 (24-Aug; stake 9.86% → 7.28%), Alpha Wave sold ~2.95 cr shares at ₹630 (28-Aug, reported full exit) and an undisclosed holder sold ~3.5 cr shares at ₹688 (21-Sep); MSCI added the stock from 1-Sep.
ownership.read: Lenskart has no controlling shareholder: the founders own ~17.5% and the largest pre-IPO funds (SoftBank 7.3% after August, ADIA, PI Opportunities Fund, Macritchie, Steadview, Unilazer) are sellers on any strength. The overhang has been absorbed well so far (the stock rose ~45% between the ₹473 block in May and the ₹688 block in September), and index inclusion (FTSE in Jun-2026, MSCI in Sep-2026) brought passive buyers. But supply will keep meeting every rally until these funds are out.

critiques: The headline EBITDA excludes rent. After rent (pre-IndAS) the margin was ~11% in FY26 and 13.3% in Q1FY27; the street's 48-58x multiples are applied to that smaller after-rent number.
India SSSG fell from 24.2% (Q4FY26) to 18.3% (Q1FY27); Equirus links part of it to negative publicity. Growth is shifting to new, smaller-town stores with lower revenue per store.
Ambit (Sell, ₹496): a capex-heavy, made-to-order model whose free cash flow lags its profit; Citi and HSBC (Neutral/Hold): the valuation already prices much of the growth.
Rupee weakness against the renminbi and yen raises the cost of imported frames and components; the product margin has held so far through in-house manufacturing.
Supply: pre-IPO funds have sold ~20% of the company since May-2026 and still hold large stakes.
Acquisitive: Owndays, Meller, Dealskart, GeoIQ and the Thailand JV in four years; ₹683 cr of IPO money is earmarked for acquisitions and general purposes.

governance.verdict: Good disclosure and a clean audit; the governance risk is not misconduct but a dispersed, exiting shareholder base and an acquisitive management whose deals are hard for outsiders to price.
